text_fidelity_a:
Vivi Electric Bike for Adults 26" Ebike, 500W Folding Electric Bike, 20MPH Adult Electric Bicycles with Removable 48V Battery, Up to 50Miles Range, Shimano 21 Speed, Dual Shock Absorber At first, the power and quickness of the electrical assist surprised me, but I got comfortable in no time. I hate to admit it, but I find myself using the electric mode (which requires no pedaling) more and more everyday. It is much like a scooter and very fun. Overall the bike handles like a cruiser and pedals with ease given 7 gear options. The shifter works well and does not get hung up too often. 

The bike is heavier with the battery but it is not that noticeable. The battery can also be removed when you know you won't be using it, or when you're charging it. It is GREAT that this has disc brakes to slow down the power of an electric bike. I kept track and for over one week, 1 hr/day, ~15 miles using assist and electric only mode, the battery indicator shows half life. It folds down to a more compact size, which is so useful if you want to transport it in your car, or fold it up for storage.  We got this initially for grandma to be able to keep up with the kids.  It turned out to be too high for her legs at the lowest setting (she's 5'1"").  My wife (5'4"") has no issues and loves using this bike with the kids. Overall, we never expected to be so won over by electric bikes; this is a great ride, and at a great price for what you're getting. There are other 'bells and whistles' included like a very loud alarm and front/back lights/accessories that add to overall biking safety and comfort.

Unboxing the bicycle was easy and the package included all the tools needed for assembly. It took about 30 minutes to put together (handle bars, seat, front wheel, fenders, pedals, air pumped into tires). There was no instruction manual in the box and the QR code led to nowhere, but I was able to find how-to videos on other similar models.  I also later found that they emailed me some tips, which were helpful.  Speaking of the seller, we contacted them because of an issue with the battery and they resolved it quickly; we were happy to see that they offered good customer service. Would be a perfect commuter's bike.
text_fidelity_b: Vivi Electric Bike for Adults 26" Ebike, 500W Folding Electric Bike, 20MPH Adult Electric Bicycles with Removable 48V Battery, Up to 50Miles Range, Shimano 21 Speed, Dual Shock Absorber

text_fidelity_a:
AURORAE Classic/Printed Extra Thick and Long Yoga Mat. Slip Free Rosin Included As a yoga beginner, I have few comparisons for this mat, except for the two classes I took before I owned the mat, in which I used mats provided by each respective yoga studio. The studio mats were of "normal" thickness, and although they were sticky enough, they were too thin. The Aurorae mat offered a significant improvement in thickness, although for some poses I still have to use additional padding, such as a blanket (but then everyone in the class is doing that, regardless of the mats they're using).

As the instructions advised, I did thoroughly wash and dry the mat before using it. I washed it with a large sponge in a bathtub filled with very warm water and a few generous squirts of dishwashing detergent. The first time I used the mat after washing it, I noticed my hands slipping a bit during downward dog, so when I got it home, I washed the mat again, and for the second washing I scrubbed the mat's surface with a soft body brush.

That seemed to help, although I suspect if you're sweaty, you'll get some slippage even when the mat's clean. I think it's important to remember to wash your hands (and feet?) before yoga practice, if you want to minimize slippage on the mat.

Overall I'm happy with the product, and I'd buy one again if I needed another mat.
text_fidelity_b: AURORAE Classic/Printed Extra Thick and Long Yoga Mat. Slip Free Rosin Included

FEND One Foldable Bike Helmet - Adult Mens and Womens Bike Helmet - Collapsible by 50% of Original Size - Safety Certified for Bicycle Road Bike Scooter Cycling Commuter Helmet… I've never been a regular wearer of helmets so I can't compare this to other brands, but this one suits me. The medium/large fits me well, and it's comfortable to wear throughout longer rides. It's also cooler than I expected, which is a real benefit as I live in a hot and often humid climate. And though it shouldn't matter, I like the simple design of this helmet as opposed to those that have a more aerodynamic look, so to speak. And I really appreciate the low-key logo; it's tasteful, not garish like you see on so many products.

But the most important thing for me is the fold. The main thing keeping me from wearing a helmet before was having to lump around a bowl. I know that's a bad reason, but it's the truth. This folds down enough to easily fit into all of my bike bags and even the small backpack that I often carry as a purse. Admittedly, it's a squeeze for the latter, and I don't carry much in that purse anyway, but the fact that it fits means that I'll use it, and using it is definitely safer than going without.

I was lucky to get a nice discount on this (for Prime Day, I think, though perhaps it was some other deal), but I think it's worth it at its regular price. Of course I hope never to give this the ultimate test, but it feels like a sound helmet and works for the way I bike. I'd definitely buy this again.

text_fidelity_a:
Delorme West Virginia Atlas This atlas is a "must-have" for anyone wishing to explore the state of West Virginia. It is a hefty atlas, with almost as many pages as a national road atlas. This is because the state is broken down into 63 pages that depict in great detail what there is to be found there.

The first page shows the entire state, along with the major roads and cities. This map is broken into rectangles, each of which represent one page in the atlas. You can use this map to get oriented and to find the page you wish to examine in greater detail. There is also a legend, which depicts the symbols and details of the map, along with some information about the design of the atlas.

Next is a comprehensive listing of place names and map features. There are charts that list points of interest along with their map coordinates so that you can find them. These include national lands, state lands, scenic drives, unique natural features, bicycle routes, historic sites, covered bridges, etc.

When you enter the map portion of the atlas, the first thing you notice is the topographic features. Mountains and valleys, rivers and lakes all stand out so as to be easily identified. If you look closely, you can actually see the topographic lines faintly drawn on the map. All roads, down to the dirt access roads are depicted, and every town is shown. And there are symbols marking the points of interest.

West Virginia is a wild and mountainous state with much to offer the traveler and adventurer, and this map makes the ideal companion for anyone who wishes to explore the state in greater detail.
text_fidelity_b: Delorme West Virginia Atlas

Taste is pretty neutral, kind of like a fig newton without the fig. Not bad at all, and not good enough that anyone is going to crave them or get into them short of a real need. This is not a gourmet meal or an enticing snack, it is not meant to provide complete nutrition, it is meant to get a person through a rough situation, and allowances have been made for that.

With the above in mind, this product earned two stars because these are so hard and so compressed that anyone without solid teeth is going to have a really difficult time eating them. They do NOT soften in liquid due to the oil content(most compact way to add calories), and the individual bars themselves are too large to be eaten without being broken apart, which may also be difficult depending on what tools and abilities a person has.

Really recommend the Datrex brand survival rations instead. All the pluses, plus easy to eat. When the chips are down and you're busting into your survival rations, there's really no reason to make it any more difficult than it already is.

Nordic Lifting Wall Ball for Crossfit & Fitness - Medicine Ball for Gym and Strength Training In my photo, I show a side-by-side comparison of a medicine ball (the Nordic Fitness ball on the left) & a slam ball (the smaller ball on the right). These are similar animals, but still very different.

Yes, they're both round & heavy. However, a medicine ball is usually (as in the case of this Nordic Fitness model) much larger & will have a slight bounce to it.

The slam ball is usually small & very dense. And normally will not bounce much (unless it's over inflated).

So while both can be used for similar exercises, if you really want to round out your routines, it's best to have both.

This medicine ball from Nordic Fitness is very well made & comes with a basic exercise guide & welcome letter.

text_fidelity_a:
NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates for Women Men Double Row Shiny Indoor Outdoor Skates for Unisex Girls with Shoes Bag [[VIDEOID:6a9dae27c4383bb5bbbf63af76ea0b65]] A year ago my wife was using roller blades, but wanting a pair of roller skates to also enjoy. A year ago, she severely broke her foot and was sidelined for seven months, but limited as she came back. Now she’s able to do more, cleared for roller blading, but she had been wanting those skates... so when I had the chance to grab her this pair, I took it. She had to wait awhile, but now she’s had a chance to get on them... These NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are decent, what she described as good for beginners and moderate skaters, but she had a few things to mention. First, she has a foot size that can be spot on 9 or 9.5 with a range that could workout between, based on the show and it's cut. In this case, ordering online, she wasn’t able to try them on first. In the end, she feels like the overall fit around the foot is good, but snug. The front of the boot - at the toes - is the tightest. She first tried with thicker socks, but settled for compression socks, which worked much better. Leather can sometimes adjust to a foot, stretching a bit to hug a foot, but in this case, we’re not sure. She says the front at the toes is tough - the leather hard - so she can’t imagine it stretching. In the end, she feels like if you’re spot on a size, you should be okay, but if there is even a slight “off” about a foot size, there could be an issue.

Second, The skates look nice, and overall the materials. - leather - seems good. The materials in the base and wheels seem good. They have wheels that are supposed to light up as they role - they do, but it’s hard to see in the light/daylight. We have not tried them in the dark, and we do see a little sparkle, but overall, you’re not going to be rolling in the dark, so what we are seeing, it’s not overly impressive. There is a little video above, but yea, the “light up” to us is not impressive. Third, She loved roller skating as a child through to young adult and wants to go back to doing it again. She loves loves loves roller blading, but there is something about skating she holds dear... We will say, her being unable to do anything like this in a year has made it hard for her - she felt it hard/big/painful and has to take this slowly getting back to it. She got up, she went, and she really liked it a lot. She felt like it’s coming back and she enjoyed the experience. She feels like these NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates are going to let her get back up and going - with time to develop - and she’s going to be able to enjoy it. But she also feels like these are beginner to moderate level. The ground itself - the surface - is important. The place we took them (parking lot) was rough and uncomfortable for her. She does have an area she loves for blading, but during several months a year (current) we have a massive amount of acorns that fall and she cannot, for safety, blade (or roller skate) in the area. So this parking lot showed her not every surface is going to work with these skates.

Overall, these ARE decent skates. Things to consider: size, type of sock, surface for skating. These will have an affect on the experience. She sets them best for beginner to moderate. And in the end, she does like them and thinks she’ll get a good amount of use out of them.
text_fidelity_b: NIKINER Women's Classic Roller Skates Premium High-top Leather Roller Skates for Women Men Double Row Shiny Indoor Outdoor Skates for Unisex Girls with Shoes Bag

text_fidelity_a:
AiRunTech Hydration Running Belt with Water Bottles, Triathlon Marathon Race Running Gear, Running Accessories for Women and Men, Gifts for Runners, iPhone Belt for Any Phone Size, Gel Holder First, a caveat: I run to get some aerobic exercise, but I am not a triathlon or marathon runner, so I haven't fully tested the limits of this running belt. For the amount and type of running that I do, the AiRunTech hydration running belt is perfect, and I suspect it also works great for the really long-distance runners.

Some features I found really useful:
- The combination of velcro adjustment plus a partially elastic band allowed me to fit the running belt exactly how I wanted it. After it's set, a buckle let's me get the belt on and off very quickly.
- The 10-oz water bottles fit securely in the belt and on my hips. The curved shape of the bottles align with the body contour better than straight bottles. An extra elastic loop makes sure each bottle stays in place and doesn't bounce.
- The main pocket fits my iphone 13 pro max securely.
- Lightweight

Additional features I didn't use:
- Earphone outlet (I use bluetooth earphones)
- Energy gel loops (the distances I run are not long enough to need energy gel)

The photos on the Amazon description page show the runners wearing the belt with the pockets and water bottles on the front part of their bodies. I didn't find the belt to be comfortable in that position--my legs hit the bottles when running. Instead, I've worn it with the pocket and bottles on my back, and then I barely notice I am wearing the belt with its bottles.

By the way, the belt works for long hikes too!

After the experience with the AiRunTech hydration running belt, I got another one for my wife that should arrive soon. This one has the smaller 6-oz. bottles.
text_fidelity_b: AiRunTech Hydration Running Belt with Water Bottles, Triathlon Marathon Race Running Gear, Running Accessories for Women and Men, Gifts for Runners, iPhone Belt for Any Phone Size, Gel Holder

Most of the helmets I've tried were too small, too heavy, straps ran weird and uncomfortable, or just plain SQUARE. The Lasor O2 fit like no other helmet I've ever tried. Another very important feature about this helmet is ....IT LOOKS COOL!! Even my niehbor who likes to make fun of cyclists because of there "pointy hats" said this one looks cool.

Don't look at another helmet. This is the best I've EVER worn. If you cycle a lot, don't hesitate. It's a bit more money but for the serious cyclist it's worth every penny. I try to ride at least 100 mile a week during the good months. If you ride simply with a family or short distances you might want to concider a cheaper model.....unless you have a big fat mellon head like me.

text_fidelity_a:
Saris Bones 805 2 Bike Trunk Mount Rack After doing a lot of research, I settled on the Saris — I didn't care about cost; I wanted something that would hold my bike secure and not scratch it or my car.

And keeping my bike secure was a huge concern. I have a 15 mile drive to where I bike out in the country — and half of that drive is on the interstate at 70+ mph.

After 6 months of use I only have praise. The Saris does in fact keep my bike secure, it doesn't scratch anything, and it's quite easy to mount to my car -- it takes me about two minutes. And it's very easy to place and secure my bike onto it.

You should be aware that it does mount to every car a bit differently. On my car the side straps mount lower than pictured on the directions because of grooves on my trunk, and I have to pop the trunk to put the lower straps in place.

My only complaint is that the front wheel will move unless you secure it with a bungee cord or velcro strap. Saris sells a separate wheel stabilizer strap; it really should just be included.

One last note: I see people who leave their Saris rack on their car all of the time. It's so easy to remove that there's really nothing to stop someone from stealing it off the back of your car when left unintended. So I always take mine off when I'm done cycling.
text_fidelity_b: Saris Bones 805 2 Bike Trunk Mount Rack

text_fidelity_a:
UVPaqlite Mini (6 x 4) I recently bought several UVPaqlite items, and have had some time to test them out. Out of the 4 items I purchased; this was the second brightest, and was the most useful size. With fair exposure to light, it will glow strong for 10 minutes. Around the 15 minute mark, it has faded a bit, but is still bright enough that you can still read with it in total darkness, with adjusted eyes. By 45 minutes, it's faintly visible in a dark room, with your eyes adjusted. By 60 and 90 minutes, the Paqlite Mini was still faintly visible, but only just barely.

It glowed brighter and longer than either the [[ASIN:B0068QL4E6 Tooblite]] and [[ASIN:B0068QN7VO Tooblite Mini]]. While the Tooblite designs are convenient for many tasks, the UVPaqlite Mini is the lightest of the bunch, and quite compact. While it doesn't seem quite as durable as the two Tooblites, the rugged vacuum-sealed packet still feels like it would hold up well to a fair amount of abuse. It also floats, slightly, compared to the Tooblites that sink like rocks. As such, I think this is the most useful of the UVPaqlite products, for my needs. I have mine in my bedroom, next to a flashlight, attached to a quick-access gun safe. In the event I'm in my room, and the lights instantly go out, I can immediately see where my flashlight is - even before my eyes have adjusted to the dark (though I also have emergency lighting for additional assistance). In a pinch, the UVPaqlite Mini is strong enough that I could find my backup flashlight, or open my safe.

Of the 4 UVPaqlite products I purchased, I'd say that this is my personal favorite. I think the combination of convenient size and brightness make it the most versatile for my needs. I intend to get more of these, and use them to tag several other handy items I'd want to be able to immediately find, in the event of a power outage. As well, they're light enough and small enough, I can easily pin them to my clothing, whenever I go outside at night and wish to remain visible. They also glow like crazy, under a UV black light, which would make them fun at parties.

With these "charge and glow" phosphorescent products, they certainly have their uses - however, they can't replace a flashlight or chemiluminescent glow stick when you need on-demand light. So, consider what you might use them for, before purchasing.
text_fidelity_b: UVPaqlite Mini (6 x 4)

Cola Bottle Vacuum Insulated Double Wall Stainless Steel Leak-proof Cola Shape Sports Water Bottle Keeps Your Drink Hot & Cold 17oz(500ml) The Skyline 17 oz premium insulated stainless steel bottle is a great choice! I own several S'Well bottles that look and function identical to this one at a MUCH lower price. A co-worker really liked my S'Well bottle but as previously stated, S'Well bottles are $25+ a bottle and that's more than I wanted to spend on a gift, so I was looking for a comparable alternative and I found it with the FLY Skyline. I wanted to make sure the Fly Skyline would keep water ice cold all day, I filled the Skyline bottle with ice cold water the before work and the bottle was effective at keeping the water ice cold the next day. The bottle is constructed of high quality stainless steel and looks/feels like it will last forever. The bottle holds 17 ounces of liquid, which is perfect for taking to work to be able to drink ice cold water at your desk. The lip on the bottle provides a very comfortable surface to drink from. The bottle includes a screw on lid that provides a leak-proof seal eliminating the worry and fear that the liquid will spill out of the bottle. The bottle states that it can keep beverages hot for 12 hours and cold for 24; I have only used the bottle for keeping beverages cold so I can only confirm that it can keep beverages cold for 24 hours (not sure about effectiveness of ability to keep beverages hot as I have not tried). The opening will easily accommodate "half moon" shaped ice but you will struggle to place ice cubes in the opening. Overall I was very satisfied with this bottle so if you are looking for a bottle that will keep your beverage hot/cold all day the Skyline stainless steel coke bottle is a great choice!

Pros:
-Keeps water cold/hot for a long time
-Stainless steel construction will last forever
-Screw top provides leak-proof seal
-Great textured surface makes holding onto bottle easy and slip free

I was fortunate enough to have received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased opinion. I would definitely purchase this bottle again.

Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series I live in an apartment in Arizona, and I wanted a quality inflatable boat I could take to the local lakes. After researching my options, IM4 appeared to be the top boat.

Although manufacturer claims it is a 4 person boat, it is NOT true. Two people can be comfortable in this boat, three is pushing it. With the semi-solid floor the boat is stable on the lakes; however, you cannot stand or dance as some reviewers claim. Solid floor allows it some degree of stability, but not enough to stand up or walk while being fully upright.

The hull materials and ores supplied are very good. Boat has a solid feel to it. When inflating it to the max, it become very firm- raft like.

For $220 this is an amazing deal. I would recommend this boat!

Update from 10/05/2012. On my recent trip to the lake I broke one of the ores. The plastic on the coupling broke when I did five spirited rows, I was upset. I had to try to canoe paddle the boat to shore and mend the plastic coupling with some duct tape! Upon returning home I checked the Intex's website for the replacement coupling; it is being sold for $4+ shipping. Can't blame the boat for the broken ore, plastic coupling is the cheapest part of this boat.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Mariner Inflatable Boat Set Series

Bodyguard Inverted Umbrella, Large Windproof Umbrellas for Rain & Sun, Compact Umbrella Reverse Umbrella with Reflective Stripe, Teflon Umbrella for Women Men, Travel Folding Umbrella with Cover Bag Every company seems to think that it can make the "next big thing" in umbrellas. It seems as though I've tried dozens of folding umbrellas that promise "this and that" but ultimately fail in one (or more) of the stated advantages. Most have some type of catastrophic failure after only a few uses, some so bad that they make the umbrella totally inoperable. So it was with some skepticism that I ordered this blue Bodyguard Travel Umbrella. It made a lot of promises on its product page -- but would it work as promised?

Finally I've found an umbrella that delivers on its promises. This Bodyguard Travel Umbrella sells for the impressive price of only $20.99, and puts a very useful collapsible umbrella in your hands. You can tell as soon as you pick it up that it is well-made and durable. It has some heft to it, snaps open with the push of a button, and collapses its canopy when you push the 'close' button. Then all you have to do is push the collapsed canopy down into the handle and your compact umbrella can be put into the supplied travel case.

The extra ribs give it additional strength when using it in the wind. It is probably more likely that it would be blown out of your hand than have the umbrella turn inside out on you. The handle is comfortable, fits my hand well, and has a wrist strap to keep it from the aforementioned potential flyaway. Yup, someone finally brought out a good one.
text_fidelity_b: Bodyguard Inverted Umbrella, Large Windproof Umbrellas for Rain & Sun, Compact Umbrella Reverse Umbrella with Reflective Stripe, Teflon Umbrella for Women Men, Travel Folding Umbrella with Cover Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer This is a simple and easy to assembly bike rack. It works perfect for us.

it took me all of 15 minutes to put together for 3 bikes. I love that you have the option to expand it to 5 bikes if needed. (more on that later). The instructions were easy to follow (I've included a pic).

What's in the box: This comes with everything you need to assemble your frame, even a little hex wrench which is the only tool you need other than your two hands. All the pieces are nicely packed in the box and have plastic over them to protect them from getting scuffed up in the box. Your box should have 2 frame tube ends, 10 frame tubes, 10 wheel arms, 5 wheel arm binders, 20 hex-head screws, and one hex wrench.

Assembly: The bottom bars for the frame pretty much snap together with little push in metal buttons to hold them in place (see pic). The holes for the buttons are nice and oblong so you have room to twist/maneuver them when attaching the wheel arms to get the holes aligned when screwing them in. The only slight issue I had is the hex screw heads. A few of them seemed to easily strip when I was doing the last few turns with the provided hex wrench. I was not even tightening them very tight so there was not a lot of torque. I figured they were probably just cheap screws, but they still did the job fine. The screws you can twist by hand easily once you get the holes aligned correctly then just use the hex wrench to finish up. Once you have the wheel arms attached the wheel arm binders easily attach at the top of the wheel arms but squeezing them together slightly then just slide the binder down next to the frame once it is on. And that's all there is to it!

using the stand: we have 3 bikes - 2 mountain bikes and 1 road bike. I thought I may have to add a spacer to the frame since the mountain bike handle bars will not fit if the two of them are right next to each other in this stand. I did try putting one in backward, with the rear wheel in the stand, but the bike stand arms were too narrow for wheel and derailer to completely fit into the stand. however, my road bike is small enough that it fits just under the mountain bike handle bars. putting that in the middle solved the issue! Now we have all three bikes neatly parked in a corner of the garage rather than leaning against the wall and boxes. yay! And if we happen to acquire more bikes, we can always expand it.

Overall this is a decent, simple bike stand that does what we need.
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Stash Rack Bike Floor Stand Bicycle Storage Organizer

text_fidelity_a:
WOW World of Watersports Zig Zag 1 or 2 Person Inflatable Towable Steerable Tube for Boating, 12-1050 Best towable we have EVER found!! This thing is super stable which is a plus for kids who are new to tubing, or who have been scared off by other tubes. The wings keep it from tipping, and also make for a very gentle landing if you need to fall off. Just roll off a wing. For those that say it is unstable, that is only really for adult riders, and you need to get your butt in the right position. Experiment. For me it is 3/4 of the way back. Lighter riders don’t seem to have that issue.
My FAVORITE part: Jumping in and out of the wake! This is what makes this tube so great! I am not strong or athletic, you just have to know the trick and COMMIT! While still straddling the middle, put ALL of your weight on one wing and pull the other wing completely off the water. If you do this slowly, you will mainly just steer within the wake. I usually do this as a warm up to make sure I feel stable. Then do it quickly!! Commit! You may need to do it back and forth quickly within the wake, but then you WILL jump it! To get back in, you need to go even quicker and COMMIT!
For those who say it splashed water, again, you are probably too far forward. Back up a bit. For those that are concerned it will hurt your legs, try this. Try sitting back on your haunches on something soft, mimicking the position you would be in on the tube. If it stresses your knees too much, it might not work for you. If not, get it! You will be fine.
It is technically a one person tube, but 2 kids, or 1 adult and 1 kid can ride on it together. I would not recommend towing an adult and child together frequently as I can see how it would stress the seems, but to help a child overcome their fear, or teach them how to jump the wake, go for it.
Durability: I weigh 200 pounds and ride it just as much, if not more, than my kids. We go boating at least 4-6 times per month in the summer, and have used it for 3 seasons now. I am hoping it is still awesome when I pull it out for this summer! Regardless, it was definitely worth the money. I plan on buying a couple more for when the one does break. I love it that much!
If you have questions about how to do something, ask. I will answer if I see the question. The only thing I haven’t figured out is barrel roles.
text_fidelity_b: WOW World of Watersports Zig Zag 1 or 2 Person Inflatable Towable Steerable Tube for Boating, 12-1050

One day, I was talking with my sister over lunch and I had noticed she pulled this water bottle from the dark recesses of her tote and nothing in her purse was wet. I was impressed. RAVE Sports Northern Lites Backcountry Snowshoe Speed Binding, Black, One Size Only the 2nd pair of snowshoes owned over the past +30 years. The old Sherpas are fine, but have been lusting over a pair of NorthernLites Backcountry for years. YOLO. Splurge. Outside of a significant weight savings, the binding system is nicer than the old Sherpas. Simple to put on or remove even with gloved hands. Only fiddling was tucking away the speed binding lace. Just in from the 4th hike. Logging an average of +9km per hike over rolling terrain in 6-12" of fresh light powder like snow. At 60kg these shoes are a bit on the too large size. Personal preference for 30"ers. The shoes track nice. Traction going up and down hill is good. Traversing a steeper face is a bit of an issue. No heel lift platform becomes an issue on longer, steeper climbs. Hit a short section of trail that was groomed for fat tire bikes. Real hard packed groomed. Shoe from some people trail runners left a minimal imprint. Left the snowshoes on for the couple hundred meters. Traction was excellent.

Expectations are for a durable product based on the past history of this brand of snowshoe.

Good for those looking for a light weight, easy on/off snowshoe for use in rolling terrain in fresh snow.

text_fidelity_a:
Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle I had a couple older magnesium stick fire starter for years and was really excited to try this out. Most people I've listened to swear by them.
Here are the PROs:
- This performs medium to well for giving you a spark. Having never used one (and probably using poor technique), I was still able to generate a decent spark at least 1 out of every 2-3 strikes.
- Doubles as a whistle. This thing actually works extremely well. If you ever need it, it's simple and high-pitched, a great space-saver.
- Feels good to use. I'd rate it at around 6 out of 10. It's a little short and I found the striker attached to the steel via the cord a little restricting, but the thumb grooves make up for it. It's funny how a small depression in plastic can make that much of a difference in comfort.

Here are the CONs:
- This requires that you have good tender or some type of fuel/accelerant. I miss having my pile of magnesium scrapings to be honest. While it's another piece of equipment, I'm probably going to keep my magnesium stick with me. It seems like the majority of times I've gone packing or camping, it's been damp out, and finding a decent amount of usable tender isn't always a sure bet.
- A little small. This is my complaint with just about any striker. They're just about a 1/4"-1/5" too small to be really comfortable. This is being picky, but still worth mentioning.

Overall, I'm enjoying using this thing and I'll probably make it a mainstay of my gear.
text_fidelity_b: Light My Fire Swedish FireSteel 2.0 Scout 3,000 Strike Fire Starter with Emergency Whistle

Pyle Sports PHRM26 Speed and Distance Heart Rate Watch with USB and 3D Walking/Running Sensor I had been afraid that the PHRM26 was going to be HUGE, like it looks in the pictures, but in actuality it is really quite reasonable in size. What seems like a 4"x3" face is more like 1¼"x1". Part of what makes it look so large is the black bump in the at the top of the watch. That bump is NOT mirrored on the bottom, and is actually INSIDE the band. What is inside the bump is a naked USB connector for plugging the watch into your computer. The connector fits into a little notch in the wristband to protect it, and the bump as actually much larger than it need be.

I had purchased the PHRM26 for it's ability to measure my heart rate. The instructions are a bit hard to follow, and there is no mention of how to activate the Heart Rate Monitor belt. APPARENTLY, you just put it on, and it works. No need to turn the belt off and on. (Makes no sense to me, the battery would last longer.)

I had a heck of a time getting the heart rate monitor to work because I was taking my cell phone with me, and it was interfering with the signal from the band. I didn't like the idea of having to leave it behind, but once I realized the problem, I used a Cell Phone Arm Band on my right arm, and kept the watch on the left arm, with my body between the two. After that it seemed to work perfectly.

Pyle Audio is a German company, and the manual is pretty poor translation into English, one that I doubt was done by a fluent English speaker. In fact, one of the most important parts of the manual was written by hand, is really in the wrong place in the manual, and gives a very slip-shod impression. Especially when you realize that the list price is well over $100! They could spend a little money and fix their manual.

Calling the included program disappointing would be an understatement of huge proportions, and is the reason why I don't give the PHRM26 a 5 star review. Oddly, it REQUIRES both a username AND password to use. In some ways this is neat, as multiple usernames allow people to SHARE the watch, as long as they exercise at different times. But the PASSWORDs can cause problems if, like me, you forget the password you used. I actually had to abandon my first username because I forgot it's password. Leaving me with an account I can neither use, nor delete. Once you get into the program itself, it's rather difficult to really make a lot of sense out of what it shows you, though it DOES allow you to both EXPORT and IMPORT CSV files that you can use in a spreadsheet program, which is nice. That allows you to keep your own records and manipulate the data in any way you see fit.

One pretty major drawback, is that the PHRM26 can only hold data for your most-recent exercise. Meaning if you forget to upload the data from the watch, the next time you exercise you will either delete the data from the previous exercise, OR you will ADD your current exercises to your last exercises, so when you finally upload the data, the current day will show the data for both days. So basically you need to upload your data every day.

The Pyle Audio (the manufacturer) website lists the PHRM26 at like $135 or something close. IMHO that is FAR above it's value. I see them regularly going for $45 - $75 in different places including Amazon, and IMHO that is STILL more than what it is worth. I was fortunate to find this one being sold by Amazon Warehouse Deals as an open package for about $25, and I feel that I paid just about the right amount for what I got. Now, the fact is that I'm a cheapskate, and I'm sure that there are many others who feel that it's worth much more, but the fact is that comparing the software that comes with the watch with the free exercise website LoseIt.com, and it's free Android app, the PHRM26 comes out very far on the low side of that comparison.
text_fidelity_b: Pyle Sports PHRM26 Speed and Distance Heart Rate Watch with USB and 3D Walking/Running Sensor

text_fidelity_a:
UP by Jawbone - Large - Mint (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I was looking for people who had similar problems with my UP and saw that several folks had the exact same problem.

First I have owned the original and the 2.0 Up. Mine has been replaced a (if you count the replacement in the works) twice. Mu husband's once. I do not shower with mine or wear it during heavy workouts. It is not very accurate on exercise, so I just log the workout and move on. We bought this because I am a programmer, and my husband is a lawyer so the fact this one reminds you to "get up and move" by buzzing is wonderful. That is about the only thing great about it. BUT it is a _big_ great since if it can save your life I don't care how many of these things I have to go through.

Now for the bad....

I thought mine was the only one that grew bigger. The band starts off fitting loose (i wear the medium), and after a few months it swells becoming tight and uncomfortable. Both bands that have failed have done so at the push button end. It stops working after some kind of firmware failure..or could be battery since it won't hold a charge, or it could be any number of things (the band itself feels mushier than when I first received it) But either way, it worked like a champ until it didn't, then an exchange of phone calls and emails with customer service results in a new band and we start over again.

There is nickel in the silver end cap (I am allergic to it) and if I forget to turn the cap around so the metal does not touch my skin I end up with a wonderful itchy rash. I have painted the ends of my cap with a clear coat of nail polish which lasts about a week before I have to repaint it, but that does fix the nickel problem. Still, with a sizable percentage of the population allergic to nickel (see fit bit recall), you would think they could design a band without it. Make the whole end silicone, or offer two caps in the package, one with the silver, one without.

I exercise regularly but either my activities are not available, or I have to take the band off to swim and it does not record biking accurately so for me the activity tracker is sort of useless. I use other systems to track swimming and biking. I have a very good bike computer and comparing UP data and the bike computer made me laugh.

The sleep tracking algorithm is really strange. It records me in bed and asleep hours before I am asleep, and sometimes does not record that I had to get up and let the dogs out at 3am. and Yes I am hitting the sleep mode making the band go "moon" as we say here. I don't believe the sleep data beyond I hit the moon and wake up and hit the sun... so it tells me the elapsed time between those two button pushes.

Other folks have commented on it, but I cook my own food and a lot of it is asian. So.... food tracker it pointless. I don't eat fast food or things with bar codes I can easily figure out the calories of. Though I do use the tracker to see how much water I have drunk in a day. This is especially helpful on campouts and hikes.

If I get a replacement for this band, I will probably give it to my son and let him wear it. I am ready to find one without nickel and that won't break after only a few months of wear.

Customer service has been terrific. Both my husband's and my replacements have been quick and easy. Though no one believes I know what I am talking about. I am a programmer, my husband is an EE and a lawyer. Please believe me when I say I have done the soft reset and it is not working. I even performed a hard reset... nada, but ok I will do it again with you on the phone...twice, and no it still is not working :-P...OK call me back in two hours when it should be charged... meh.

I have other things to do with my time like make some $$ so I can buy a different band that will work for longer than a few months at a time.

In the end it is a good idea just not executed well.
text_fidelity_b: UP by Jawbone - Large - Mint (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641 I have gone back to a wheel gun for concealed carry because I can't afford the one time that I might need to use my defensive weapon and have it jam. I know, I know! The modern semi autos are basically fool proof and malfunctions only happen occasionally. And I know that even with a subcompact you can easily carry 8-10 rounds of whatever, but I learned a long time ago that the more moving parts in any machine/tool, the more potential problems can happen -- and usually at the worst possible time. (Thank you Mr. Murphy).

My new defensive carry is a Smith & Wesson Model 327 2" Performance Center that holds eight rounds of 38 Special/ 38 +P/357 Magnum. It is a rather large revolver made of scandium and has a large grip which fits my hand perfectly. I'm a big guy so it's really no problem to conceal and the 2" barrel should make it qualify (in court) as a defensive weapon should I have to use it. My backup is a Ruger LCR in 357, a light and tiny gun that is a devil to shoot full power loads in. Fortunately I'm a big fan of 44 magnums and am comfortable handling a lot of recoil. Why the Ruger LCR as backup? There's nothing like redundancy in personal defense. A second gun using the same ammo covers most of the bases.

The result is that I can carry two revolvers loaded with a total of 13 rounds -- equaling or surpassing any of the subcompact/compact autos -- that will both go "Bang" when needed. And, and this is a big "And", any family member or passerby will also be able to operate either one of them should I be in trouble/incapacitated. All you have to do is pull the trigger. The alternative is a semi auto that might pose operating difficulty to whomever tries to be of assistance. There won't be enough time to lecture anyone on the operating mechanics of a semi auto.

So I picked up two QuickStrips and this pouch. Putting in two of the strips, one facing up and one facing down, creates a relatively slim package holding an additional ten rounds -- on top of the thirteen already loaded in the two revolvers. The total of 23 rounds should be enough for 99% of the potential situations encountered in most areas. I try to keep myself out of dangerous areas/predicaments (situational awareness), but if I have to enter one I will have a Glock 19 as my backup. A good man knows his limitations.
text_fidelity_b: TUFF Double Quick Strip Pouch, Fits 6357 7357 1022 544 644 641

text_fidelity_a: Rough Rider Folder Denim Micarta RR2181 I have a soft spot for traditional folding knives.  And Wharncliffes.. This is both.  It's also a good quality, super sharp, stainless slipjoint folder with a half stop and a Micarta handle.  For 20 bucks (or at least that's around what I paid for it).  This knife is at  a sweet spot in terms of size.  Any larger and it would start to need a clip and sort of cease to be "pocket friendly".  I mean what else can I say.. I was skeptical of the Rough Rider brand but they really are well made for the money.  I also bought a peanut for my wife and it, too is built to a high standard.  For some folks, half stops are a must.  I generally find them irritating and that may be my only gripe with this blade.  The nail nicks are too sharp to put half stops in this blade.  The blade starts to shift into the half stop and the nick twists and sometimes breaks the edge of my thumbnail.  I thought I was imagining this so i tried it with my pointer finger and sure enough, after pulling the blade a few times, the edge of my fingernail would break.  I may file or polish the edge of the nick a bit and that would solve the issue.  The blade sticks out enough that I can just grab it most of the time without the nail nick.  A slight thumb cutout on one scale would improve this .  Oh, and I could do without it being stainless.  I greatly prefer sharpening carbon steel, but that's just personal preference. Overall this knife will be a great work knife and would delight any wood worker.
text_fidelity_b: Rough Rider Folder Denim Micarta RR2181

I like the large handle to hold on to, that being said it is plastic and appears sturdy. I can also carry other things and hold on to the lantern due to the large handle. It is lightweight the lens covers at each end are plastic. It looks rugged and tough. The on and off buttons and the USB port (to charge the flashlight/lantern and your phone) are under the handle very convenient and also convenient to change the lighting while walking. When charging the Flashlight/lantern the blue led lights under the handle show the charging and make for a nice night light when charging. I love it for around the house and a must have for the car..the flashing red lights may come in handy. Still not sure about the camping durability if you are the Paul Bunion type ... but for me it is perfect and I am happy I have it on my bedside at night. Oh it came with a tripod perfect for sitting up on a table etc.. while camping out? drawing the bugs away while providing plenty of light for you to have a picnic a safe distance away.

text_fidelity_a:
POLAR V800 GPS Sports Watch/Running Watch with Heart Rate Monitor, Black This is the absolute worst training watch I have ever used and infuriates me to no end. Quick overview. I am a professional athlete, i train 6 days a week, usually twice a day. I take good care of my equipment. I rinse the watch after most workouts as directed. I do not swim with it. I do not sleep with it on. I do not wear it throughout the day. I use it for running, skiing, strength training. I am not hard on it, I do not throw it around. I have gone through 6 of these watches in less than 1 year. THEY ALMOST NEVER CONSISTENTLY SYNC VIA BLUETOOTH OR COMPUTER CABLE. I have a new iPhone 6S, and Macbook Pro. No issues with them at all, ever, except for f***ing syncing this watch.
Do not waste your money. The timer works great, the hr is great, the gps is great, the modes are awesome, the morning orthostatic test is awesome, I love everything about this watch. But the fact that it fails 19 times out of 20 tries whenever I try to sync it makes it utterly useless. I f***ing hate using this watch. Buy a Suunto or a Garmin. Just do it. Do not waste your money on this. You will get frustrated, you will get infuriated. I keep sending this watch back to be "fixed". Sometimes they try and fix it, other times I get a brand new watch in plastic. Literally. And then a week later it stops syncing.
Buy a Suunto or a Garmin. The syncing feature and flowsync software for this watch is awful and years behind the competitors. I bought a Garmin for back up and much prefer using it. My garmin (forerunner 610 used from ebay) never has an issue and syncs in about 10 seconds. It takes 5 minutes for the polar v800 to sync and it fails 19 times out of 20. Such a waste of time, especially if you're busy and spending 45 minutes of your evening swearing at your stupid polar watch that won't upload your workouts to your computer or phone.
DO NOT BUY THIS WATCH, WASTE OF MONEY, FOR THIS MONEY BUY A SUUNTO OR GARMIN!
You have been warned. If you buy this and end up pissed off waiting for the thing to work, then you'll remember reading this and knowing it was a waste of money.

text_fidelity_a: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed I quite love this blade.. I bought the coated version to leave in my car as a utility knife, but very quickly it found its way into my pockets.. There are a few issues with this knife:  I had to immediately borrow a star key tool to change the clip over to the tang.. I don't really care if it carries tip up or down (comes tip down) but the clip is a bit large on this knife and just in the way, particularly for a knife with such great ergonomics.  The coating on the blade is also not the best.. Also mine had a few little imperfections throughout the blade- just a little pitting here and there.  Still, pretty quickly this knife has made it into my rotation.  The main reason is its ease of use.  The washers have worn in quite well and though it was a bit stiff out of the box, within a week, it opens like butter.. I've typically always favored old-school slipjoint pocket knives over locking knives for carry, but i really see the ease of one-hand use in this design.  The weight and size of the blade also really add to the inertia upon opening so it's just a really satisfying knife to flip open.. Other people might balk at the grips- I thought they felt a little cheap in the hand when I first inspected the knife, but they've turned out to be pretty solid, textured just enough to prevent slippage if they got wet.  Is it the best knife for the money?  I don't know- I bought mine for around 15 bucks and at that price wasn't expecting much:  Just a decent linerlock with a soft enough blade to easily keep sharp- something for the car-  but its size, ease of use and just good solid blade design make for a really practical tool knife which i carry more and more.
text_fidelity_b: Ontario Knife Rat-1 Knife, 5in. Closed

It fastens into two brackets (the brackets are fastened to two of the legs of the trampoline) with those little pop out pins... you know the kind you squeeze to push them down and then the bar can be pushed into the bracket and then the pins pop out through little holes to hold the handle bar on. Yes it holds the handle bar on but it is a little wobbly and if you have any type of stability issues already it could take a little while to build up trust.  I cannot use the trampoline without holding onto the bar and I haven’t had any problems yet but it’s just taking some time for me to trust it LOL  For the average person I doubt that this would be even a thought but like I said for me personally I would prefer the handlebar to be a little more solid feeling. Do I use it yes! Am I enjoying it yes! Will it be up for sale in six months no!  I chose this particular one because I wanted springs rather than the bungee type cords that could wear out faster  It does make a little spring noise but if you have music going you’re not going to notice it at all. The jump area was larger than expected and very nice. I am getting serious workouts on this thing with very limited movements on my part.  Putting it together was super simple it came in a taco shape and you just opened it up and then lifted the legs up and they went into place. The instructions did note to be careful when I unfolding which I did not read and I did smash my finger LOL my instructions showed a different stability bar that had bolts to hold it in.  I don’t know if that was for an older model or what but it makes me kind a wish that the handle did fasten with bolts.  Don’t be scared of my negativity though as far as the handle goes I am only reviewing this on how I feel about it for my own personal use and like I said I do have very restricted mobility and balance.  I would recommend this to others. You can get a serious workout in 20 to 30 minutes. For those of you wondering about the size; if you are familiar with the round Costco dog beds it’s about the same size as that.
text_fidelity_b: ANCHEER Fitness Exercise Trampoline with Handle Bar, 40" Foldable Rebounder Cardio Workout Training for Adults or Kids (Max. Load 300lbs, Zero Stretch Jump Mat) (Green)
